races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Irish Stallion Farms EBF (C & G) Maiden

runners_data.name: Bold Move
runners_data.note: Trainer Donnacha O'Brien and jockey Gavin Ryan is a strong combination, but two previous runs at Goodwood produced 6th and 7th in fair company — a genuine hold-up operator who will find himself operating further forward than ideal given the field size; style fit penalises its chances in a shape controlled by the front end.

runners_data.name: Capability Brown
runners_data.note: One run to date, 6th over 8f at Goodwood for the powerful A P O'Brien yard — Jack Cleary's 5lb claim softens the weight burden, but this horse needs to settle deep and will be shuffled forward against its instincts by an 18-runner field; going is fine but the positional compromise is real.

runners_data.name: Closefield Beau
runners_data.note: Two starts for Daniel McLoughlin, finishing 7th and 10th at Goodwood, with the 10th coming on soft ground on his most recent start — that soft-going run is not encouraging, and Nathan Crosse will be managing a horse pressed into a more prominent role than it naturally seeks.

runners_data.name: Consenza
runners_data.note: Noel Meade runner with one run to date, 8th at Goodwood, and is tagged as a fader in the closing stages — the combination of that tendency and the forced midfield position rather than its natural hold-up berth makes it difficult to construct a winning narrative here.

runners_data.name: Dawnmore
runners_data.note: Unraced for J S Bolger and Seamie Heffernan — Bolger is a master at producing well-tuned debutants, and Heffernan's booking is a clear upgrade signal; completely unknown stylistically (marked U) but this pairing on soft ground at 7f is not to be dismissed lightly.

runners_data.name: Drumbeat
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan rides this A P O'Brien juvenile who ran 3rd over 8f and 6th over 7f at Goodwood — a genuine prominent-racing type who will get his position just off Equus Victor and is the horse most naturally placed to capitalise if the leader weakens; going is fine.

runners_data.name: Power Through
runners_data.note: Debut runner for A Oliver, drawn here with Gary Carroll in the saddle — no form to analyse, unknown style, and the trainer's 14-day strike rate (0/12) offers limited confidence; must be respected as an unknown but there is no positive angle to attach.

runners_data.name: Snapequus
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien runner, one run at Goodwood producing an 11th-place finish with a fading-in-finish tag — Declan McDonogh is a positive booking but the debut was uninspiring and the fade tendency on similar ground is a concern over 7f soft.

runners_data.name: The Captains Day
runners_data.note: One debut run at Goodwood finishing 4th over 7f for M D O'Callaghan with Colin Keane — fourth on debut is a solid platform, Keane is among the best in Ireland, and the unknown style tag leaves tactical options open; going is fine and this is one of the more interesting profile horses.

runners_data.name: Verona Basilica
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's hold-up type ran 9th over 8f at Stamford — Chris Hayes takes the ride, but the fading tendency and a step back in trip to 7f on soft ground are not obviously helpful; the field size will push this horse further forward than it wants.

runners_data.name: Moon Sand
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's runner had two efforts both producing 9th, over 8f at Goodwood each time — a fader ridden without a named jockey here, ran just three days ago which is an unusually tight turnaround; fatigue on soft ground is a real concern.

runners_data.name: Don't Go Mad
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's two-year-old with one run producing a distant 15th over 6f at Goodwood — the trip extension to 7f and switch to soft is a logical trainer manoeuvre, but the debut was poor and the trainer's 14-day strike rate (0/19) is cold; hard to make a case.

runners_data.name: Equus Victor
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner ridden by Ben Coen for Daniel James Murphy — has form over a variety of trips and going, with soft-ground experience (1/2 on similar ground), and the tactical gift of being unopposed at the head of affairs in a large field is significant; the key question is whether his soft-ground stamina holds over 7f.

runners_data.name: Forthethrillofit
runners_data.note: Paddy Harnett's 3lb claim is useful, and this is a Donnacha O'Brien debutant — completely unknown in terms of style and ability, but the powerful yard knows what it has at home; the soft conditions and 7f trip are not unusual parameters for an O'Brien juvenile.

runners_data.name: How Now
runners_data.note: Conor Maxwell's unknown debutant ridden by James Ryan — the trainer has a very small book (0/4 over 14 days) which provides minimal confidence, and without any stylistic pointer this is largely speculative; soft ground on debut is a demanding ask.

runners_data.name: Invincible Mind
runners_data.note: J M Sheridan partners this Joseph Patrick O'Brien first-timer — the yard's 14-day strike rate (12/72) is among the strongest in the field and gives the debutant an obvious positive angle; completely unexposed so the style and ability question is open, but the trainer angle is real.

runners_data.name: King Paddy
runners_data.note: Paul Flynn's runner finished 12th and 17th in two starts, both fading — Leigh Roche rides, but the form reads poorly, the fading tendency is confirmed, and the drop to 7f with soft conditions does not solve the core issue.

runners_data.name: Lamar River
runners_data.note: Shane Foley rides for Daniel O'Sullivan, who has no 14-day winners — two runs produced 5th and 6th at Stamford and the Curragh on similar soft-ish ground (1/2), which gives mild soft-going encouragement; the long 158-day absence is the significant question mark, and natural hold-up style means traffic will be an issue.

races.paceDynamic: Equus Victor is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner 7f soft-ground maiden and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure him, Ben Coen can dictate a sustainable, unhurried gallop from the front — a significant positional advantage on soft going at Gowran. Drumbeat is the only other runner with a confirmed prominent style and will likely settle just off Equus Victor's shoulder, meaning the pace is structured rather than strong and the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching. The redistribution note is important here: Consenza, Closefield Beau, Capability Brown, Bold Move, and several other natural hold-up horses will find themselves shuffled into midfield by the sheer size of the field and the absence of a pace-pressing rival, meaning the race shape will be set by the front end with a bunched, traffic-heavy mid-division. A soft gallop from a single leader on testing ground unambiguously favours the horse or horses who can travel prominently and sustain their effort to the line — positional types able to be covered up just behind Equus Victor, or the leader himself if he controls the tempo shrewdly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Equus Victor Dictates Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Equus Victor is allowed a clean, uncontested lead through the first half with no horse willing to pressurise him from wide or off the pace.
scenarios.body: On soft ground at 7f, a lone leader controlling his own fractions is in an enviable position — the remainder of the field must absorb a slow-burn gallop and produce a finish from off the bridle, which penalises horses stuck in traffic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Equus Victor's soft-ground stamina wanes in the final furlong and a prominent horse tracks him to the line and overpowers him.
scenarios.body: Drumbeat and any unknown debutant who secures a forward pitch would be perfectly placed to swoop as the leader empties, benefiting from a compressed gallop that leaves the field coiled and primed for one surge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutant Bolts Up
scenarios.trigger: If one of the well-bred first-time-out runners (Dawnmore, Forthethrillofit, Invincible Mind, How Now) is significantly better than anything seen in this race and produces an eye-catching performance fresh.
scenarios.body: Seven furlongs on soft for a big-yard juvenile making a debut is a classic scenario for a debut winner; with a moderate pace set by Equus Victor, an unexposed horse grabbing a prominent early position could sprint clear before rivals can pick up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Emerge Through Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely in the closing stages and horses from deep in the field thread through beaten rivals to fill the places.
scenarios.body: This scenario is structurally unlikely given that the true hold-up types have been redistributed into midfield and face a traffic-heavy passage, making a sustained late run from the rear difficult to execute; only a dramatic pace collapse would bring them into play.

watchPoints.text: Watch Equus Victor's stride pattern in the opening two furlongs — if Ben Coen is allowed to establish a length or more uncontested, this race shape is set and the tempo becomes his to control entirely.
Drumbeat's early positioning battle with Equus Victor will define the race: if Wayne Lordan pushes to lead rather than track, the pace immediately accelerates and transforms the entire shape.

Moon Sand ran just three days ago and returns on soft ground — if this horse shows any sign of fatigue or greenness in the early stages, it could cause traffic disruption for the midfield group behind it.

The cluster of hold-up horses (Consenza, Capability Brown, Bold Move, Closefield Beau) will be seeking gaps simultaneously in the final 2f — watch for a bunching incident at the quarter-mile pole as 18 runners compress in a soft-ground finish.

Dawnmore (Bolger/Heffernan) and Forthethrillofit (D O'Brien/Harnett) are the debutants most worth tracking from the stalls — early prominent positioning by either would immediately elevate their chance from speculative to live contender.

races.name: 1xBet.ie Proud Supporters Of Irish Racing Handicap

runners_data.name: Snow Light
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Standard-to-Slow at Dundalk suggesting some stamina base, but 278 days off the track is a major fitness question for Hogan's filly; genuine front-runner who will attempt to lead, likely facing a fierce duel with Motta Alta and others.|
runners_data.comment: Snow Light won last time out and has run over today's trip, giving her a solid profile, but 278 days off the track is the clear concern heading into this.

runners_data.name: Lohoobb
runners_data.note: Lee takes over on a three-year-old who finished first over 7f at Goodwood and has consistent form in the 6-7f range; a genuine hold-up horse whose soft-ground profile is sound and who is well-placed if the pace collapses as expected — only 20 days since last run suggests freshness.|
runners_data.comment: Lohoobb won last time out and, with experience over today's trip and a fine edge in our ratings, he looks a genuine threat here; the main risk is whether 142 lb from stall 12 blunts his momentum.

runners_data.name: Motta Alta
runners_data.note: Harrington's filly has a soft-ground win at 7f and two other placed efforts on similar going, making her the pace-setter with the strongest credentials for today's conditions; Foley is booked and she goes forward, but whether she can control the gallop with four others pressing is the key question.|
runners_data.comment: Motta Alta shaped well when third last time out, and a winner two starts back, hinting at a filly in good heart; she has run over today's trip and going, and her rating of 88 makes her the one to beat here, albeit the 139 lb burden is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Solana Beach
runners_data.note: Heffernan takes the mount on a mare placed twice on soft ground who has a tidy 2/3 similar-going record; a naturally prominent racer who needs to avoid being swallowed into the pace war, and her second over 7f on soft is directly relevant form.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, Solana Beach has nonetheless shown consistent placing form — second and third among those efforts — and has run over today's distance and going before; the 81-day absence and 138 lb burden are the questions she must answer here.

runners_data.name: Friendly Invoice
runners_data.note: Long 200-day absence is a serious concern for Maxwell's runner, and the flag noting a tendency to fade in the finish only amplifies doubts; Whearty rides, and while there is a win in the form string, all relevant runs were over 6f on Standard-to-Slow rather than genuine soft.|
runners_data.comment: Friendly Invoice makes her return after a 200-day absence and ranks tenth of twelve on our figures, making her hard to fancy at this level; she does bring distance and going experience and showed ability when winning three starts back, but the lengthy layoff is a significant concern.

runners_data.name: Girl Bear
runners_data.note: Jack Foley's filly has a modest form profile with limited placed efforts and no wins, and her best effort came over 8f on Good suggesting stamina helps her; Leigh Roche rides, and a hold-up run from the back is the plan, though the soft ground and sharp pace may actually suit her grinding style.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with an eighth last time out and a seventh before that, Girl Bear faces a stiff ask from stall four, though her experience over today's trip and going and a return to action after 36 days at least gives connections something to work with.

runners_data.name: Cladach
runners_data.note: O'Brien's runner is a true hold-up horse in terms of racing style — shown in the midfield slot here only because the rear is oversubscribed with hold-up types, and that positional squeeze may compromise its chance; has faded in four consecutive runs including a tenth from ten, so raw form is deeply unencouraging despite the trainer's powerful strike rate.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with an eighth and an unplaced effort in recent outings, Cladach looks hard to fancy on these figures, ranked 11 of 12 in the field; has run over today's trip before, and at least returns on a sharp turnaround of just 10 days.

runners_data.name: Glasarmi
runners_data.note: Ryan partners a front-runner who contested a soft-ground race and placed at 5/7f on similar going, though a 25th-place finish last time out at Goodwood is alarming; Devine's runner will press the early pace but looks likely to be among those that crack rather than the one who survives.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Glasarmi is hard to fancy, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick ten-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Star Strewn
runners_data.note: Farrell's gelding has headgear listed and returns after 130 days off, with a win and third at 7f on Standard; Cleary rides and he will press forward, but his single soft-ground run produced only a fifth and the layoff means fitness is not guaranteed.|
runners_data.comment: Star Strewn won three starts back but has since finished eighth and ninth, and 130 days off the track is a significant fitness question; she has run over today's trip and carries 136 lb from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Ninth Crusade
runners_data.note: Keane picks up the ride for O'Callaghan on a horse who ran just yesterday — a very tight turnaround that is a significant physiological flag; hold-up in style, his 2/8 similar-going record is modest, but Colin Keane's judgment in running can compensate for limited form if the pace fully falls apart.|
runners_data.comment: Ninth Crusade is yet to win in his last five starts, though a third and a second among his recent efforts offer some encouragement; the concern is that he returns just one day after his latest unplaced effort, which makes a bounce-back harder to fancy.

runners_data.name: Nazario
runners_data.note: Murtagh's runner goes in a tongue-tie and has modest 6f form on soft with a placed effort at 6f on Standard; Ben Coen rides and a prominent position is the plan, though stepping up to 7f soft may expose a stamina limitation given the horse's form has been predominantly at shorter distances.|
runners_data.comment: Nazario shaped with promise when runner-up five starts back and our rating of 83 puts him firmly in contention from stall 2, with experience over today's trip adding to his claims; the concern is a trainer without a winner in 27 attempts over the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Venetian Star
runners_data.note: Has two placed efforts on soft going including a second over 7f, which gives her a relevant form angle for today; a front-runner by style who will add to the pace war, but 11th and 10th in recent runs and a 14-day turnaround suggest McAteer will need a significant improvement to be competitive.|

races.paceDynamic: Snow Light, Motta Alta, Star Strewn, and Glasarmi are all confirmed front-runners, with Venetian Star adding a fifth pace-pressing presence, creating a near-certain fierce gallop from the off on soft ground over seven furlongs at Gowran. This volume of pace means the leaders will burn each other out through a testing middle section, with the soft going ensuring every stride extracts a physical toll and eroding any lead advantage long before the final two furlongs. Cladach is a genuine hold-up type redistributed into the midfield position on this map because the field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural station — Snow Light and Motta Alta are most likely to actually lead, with Star Strewn and Glasarmi likely harassing them and burning petrol early. This race shape strongly favours genuine hold-up and late-finishing profiles who can absorb the pace collapse in the closing stages, with prominent types who conserve energy early also well-placed if they avoid the pace battle entirely.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the five pace-pressers set a genuinely fierce early gallop and the soft ground forces a mass capitulation in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The leaders burn out on testing ground, opening a clear lane for horses tracking further back; genuine stamina becomes the decisive quality in the final furlong. Hold-up horses with strong finishes and proven soft-ground form are ideally positioned to collect.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Sits Off Pace
scenarios.trigger: If one prominently-ridden runner settles just behind the pace war and pounces when the front-runners crack at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A runner like Solana Beach or Nazario, content to travel without leading, avoids the early speed duel and hits the front at the right moment with something in reserve. Soft-ground form and a willingness to race off the bridle in the closing stages are the critical credentials here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the confirmed leaders — most likely Motta Alta given her soft-ground win — dictates a controlled rhythm and the pace war subsides early enough to preserve stamina.
scenarios.body: Motta Alta's 1W2P record on similar going gives her a genuine profile edge if she can seize a comfortable lead while rivals check each other; soft ground at Gowran does occasionally reward an economical front-runner who avoids a sustained duel. The scenario requires the other pace horses to be checked or outpaced early, which is plausible if Foley dictates terms aggressively from the gate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is hot but not catastrophic and a horse from a mid-pack position sustains a long, grinding run through the final three furlongs on the testing ground.
scenarios.body: Cladach, the true hold-up type mapped to midfield, could theoretically benefit if the pace is strong enough to string the field out and O'Brien's charge produces a sustained effort — though the style-fit discount and recent poor form temper confidence. Girl Bear or another midfield passenger could also profit if the pace collapses uniformly and the winner comes from a middle draw grinding late.

watchPoints.text: Five confirmed front-runners — Snow Light, Motta Alta, Star Strewn, Glasarmi, and Venetian Star — will create an almost certain pace war; watch which of them weakens first in the final two furlongs, as the order of collapse will determine the race shape entirely.

Ninth Crusade ran yesterday and Colin Keane takes over — the one-day turnaround is extreme and must be monitored in pre-race, as a horse running back-to-back on soft ground is a physiological risk regardless of trainer intention.

Cladach, a genuine hold-up type repositioned on this map, has faded in all four recent starts — if the pace is as strong as projected, the closing opportunity may materialise but the horse's own finishing tendency means it may not capitalise even with a clear run.

Friendly Invoice returns after 200 days off with a finish-fading flag on a notoriously stamina-testing combination of soft ground and 7f; watch the market closely — if there is no confidence money, the layoff concern is likely confirmed.

Motta Alta is the most interesting pace angle: her soft-ground win gives Shane Foley something to aim at, and if she jumps cleanly and establishes a clear lead before the pace war intensifies, she has the form to sustain it longer than her rivals — watch her early position out of the gates.

races.name: Membership At Gowran Park Fillies Claiming Race

runners_data.name: Quinta Girl
runners_data.note: Recent form shows she handles soft and has placed over 6-7f in similar conditions, but her natural deep hold-up style is squeezed out by the density of closers in this field — she is effectively racing from midfield rather than the rear, which blunts her trademark late surge and tempers her winning chance.|
runners_data.comment: Quinta Girl has been placed third two starts back and shaped with promise in recent starts, and she has run over today's distance and going before; winless in her last five, the 74-day absence is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Tax Me Later
runners_data.note: Rated OR 120, significantly highest-rated runner in this claiming field, and placed on her only run over this trip on good ground; if that form translates to soft she has the class to dominate, but the single run and absence of soft-going evidence make her a fascinating but uncertain quantity.|
runners_data.comment: Tax Me Later shaped with promise when third last time out, has run over today's trip, and her speed rating of 91 gives her a strong case from stall four; the main risk is that she remains yet to score and must convert that potential into a win here.

runners_data.name: Star Of Beauty
runners_data.note: Consistent record of placing at 8f on good ground — two seconds, a third — gives her a clear trip profile that suits this mile; switching from good to soft is the key question but she handles the step up in class regularly and W J Lee gives her a strong pilot.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with back-to-back sixth-place finishes most recently, Star Of Beauty is hard to fancy on a rating ten pounds below official, though she has run over today's trip and the placed efforts earlier in this sequence hint at some ability.

runners_data.name: Profit Surge
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has to fight Minaun View for the lead from the off; her soft-going exposure is very limited (1 run, no win) and burning energy in a duel on testing ground is a significant concern despite Colin Keane's ability to dictate terms.|
runners_data.comment: Profit Surge has run over today's trip and arrives on the back of a win last time out, but her recent record also shows a string of placed efforts without always converting, and 128 lb from stall 1 adds a further test of her claims.

runners_data.name: Keep It Together
runners_data.note: Raised a fade-in-finish flag which is telling given the step back to a mile from much longer trips — this veteran (8yo) has been running over 12-16f on good ground and the drop in distance and switch to soft are both unfamiliar; hold-up style with no recent soft-ground wins makes this tough.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with back-to-back sixths her best recent efforts, Keep It Together ranks eighth of nine on our figures and faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip before and returns on a sound 17-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Minaun View
runners_data.note: Two wins over 8f gives her proven course-and-distance credentials, and she has been busy (5d since last run) but trainer McGuinness has a decent recent strike rate; tongue-strap helps, and if she outguns Profit Surge for the lead she becomes a serious player on her best form.|
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back yet fifth last time out, Minaun View has experience over today's trip and going but returns just five days later, and her draw eight and 127 lb burden may make life tough for a filly ranked sixth of nine.

runners_data.name: Salamina
runners_data.note: Fades-in-finish tag is damning given a form string of four consecutive zeros; Joseph Patrick O'Brien sends her here but the prior form on good over longer trips shows no ability to land a blow, and soft ground adds further burden to an already struggling profile.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Salamina faces a stiff ask from 132 lb out of stall six, though the seven-day turnaround suggests connections believe she retains fitness.

runners_data.name: Vlhova
runners_data.note: The one confirmed winner among the hold-up types (7 wins/places from 15 soft-going runs showing reasonable adaptability), and placed twice at 7-8f in softer conditions; tongue-strap fitted and the 35-day break is mildly concerning, but she stays the trip and has shown class on a similar surface.|
runners_data.comment: Twice placed three and four starts back, Vlhova heads here on a 35-day break with distance and going experience in her favour, and an 80 rating that just edges her to the top of these; winless in her last five, she needs to convert that placed form into something more decisive.

runners_data.name: Una Matata
runners_data.note: Won over 7f at Sligo on a standard surface and placed at the same trip — the step to 8f on soft is a slight unknown but she sits in a prominent style that suits the likely pace scenario; trainer McGuinness runs her alongside Minaun View suggesting yard confidence, and Adam Caffrey's claim brings the weight down.|
runners_data.comment: Una Matata showed smart form when winning five starts back, and her experience over today's distance and going keeps her firmly in the mix carrying 129 lb from stall nine; the main risk is a 67-day absence leaving her short of peak fitness.

races.paceDynamic: Profit Surge and Minaun View are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead from flag, creating a genuinely contested pace over the mile on soft ground at Gowran. With two horses fighting for the same piece of real estate, neither can settle comfortably, and the resulting honest-to-brisk gallop on a softening surface is likely to prove punishing on the front pair as they enter the straight. Prominent types who can sit just off the speed — Star Of Beauty, Tax Me Later, Una Matata — are best positioned to benefit, tracking the contest without burning energy in the early tussle, then hitting the rising ground with something in reserve. This race shape structurally favours a close-tracking prominent racer who can let the duel unfold ahead and pounce inside the final two furlongs. The field also holds more hold-up types than the pace map can place at the rear: Quinta Girl is a genuine deep closer but is effectively mapped to midfield given the glut of hold-up horses, meaning she is unlikely to secure her ideal position and her chance must be discounted accordingly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Burns Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Profit Surge and Minaun View push each other through an unrelenting early pace, the close-tracking prominent types inherit a race run to suit them.
scenarios.body: The front two sap each other's reserves on soft ground, and a horse sitting three or four lengths off the pace in a prominent position can cruise into contention turning in and pick up the weakening leaders; Star Of Beauty's record of placing at this trip on good ground translates well if the soft absorbs the front-runners' energy first.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Pinches It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace-setters establishes a clear advantage early and the other capitulates or settles, the remaining leader dictates a controlled but honest tempo and outstays the field.
scenarios.body: Minaun View's recent course-and-distance form (winning over 8f) makes her the more likely candidate to dominate if Profit Surge cannot match her early stride; Colin Keane on Profit Surge is the obvious counter, and if he seizes the initiative from the off he can dictate a rhythm that blunts all closers on the soft surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly brutal and the prominent horses are also compromised, a horse delivered from midfield with a powerful sustained run can pick off a tiring field.
scenarios.body: Quinta Girl, though mapped to midfield rather than her natural deep position, has soft-ground form and could benefit if the race becomes a true test of stamina; Vlhova has placed multiple times over similar trips and could get into it with a well-timed run from the same position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Tactical Race
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners sense the other and ease off, producing a false or slow early pace that turns the race into a sprint finish from the home turn.
scenarios.body: In this unlikely shape the field concertinas and luck-in-running becomes decisive; horses with tactical speed like Tax Me Later or Star Of Beauty would be best placed to respond to a sudden injection of pace, while pure hold-up types would find a wall of horses ahead of them.

watchPoints.text: Minaun View and Profit Surge will clash for the lead from the off — watch the opening two furlongs to see which concedes, as whoever wins that battle shapes the entire race.|

Tax Me Later's OR of 120 is comfortably the highest in the field and on a straight-class reading she should be hard to beat, but her single run and no soft-going record mean she could underperform if the ground really bites.|
Keep It Together and Salamina both carry fade-in-finish flags — if either is prominent early rather than settled at the back, they are likely to stop badly in the straight and cause interference.|

Quinta Girl has not run for 74 days and her natural hold-up style is compromised by the race shape — monitor the market; if she is heavily supported she may have been working well at home, but tactically she faces a difficult day.|

Una Matata is stablemate to Minaun View under the same trainer (McGuinness, T14: 2/21) — if Minaun View sets a strong pace, Una Matata's prominent style could allow her to travel smoothly just behind her own stable's pacesetter and strike late.|

races.name: Societies Welcome At Gowran Park Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Navajo Point
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator whose recent form reads poorly with a series of fading efforts, and sim-going returns of 0W0P from eight attempts undermine confidence; 17 days since last run is not a concern but the finishing pattern is.|
runners_data.comment: Navajo Point arrives here 17 days fresh, has run over today's trip and going, and that runner-up last time out puts him in decent heart; winless in his last five starts yet drawn in stall two carrying 142 lb, his latest effort makes him a compelling each-way proposition.

runners_data.name: Selective Power
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type with the best soft-going strike rate in the field (10/15, 1W2P) and a recent soft placing at 8f that directly matches today's conditions; 81 days off is the main query.|
runners_data.comment: Selective Power has shown glimpses of ability with two fourth-place finishes in his last five starts, and he has run over today's distance and going before, but 81 days off the track is a concern and he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Volendam
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, rated 60 and carrying 142lbs with Jessica O'Gorman's claiming allowance; has raced prominently but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.94) and a lone soft-ground run without a win tempers its chance of lasting, though no rival is likely to press it.|
runners_data.comment: Volendam ran a solid second two starts back and has experience of today's distance and going in her favour, with 29 days since her last run suggesting she returns fresh; the unplaced effort last time out is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Medieval Night
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Denis Hogan (2/25 over 14 days) whose form figures on soft are moderate (8/15, 0W0P) and whose recent runs at shorter trips on good ground haven't been encouraging; the step up in trip could help.|
runners_data.comment: Medieval Night has shown flashes of ability — placed second last time out and third six starts back — but a sixth and seventh in between highlight his inconsistency, and he remains yet to win in recent starts; 141 lb from stall 15 adds to the challenge.

runners_data.name: Mags
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who won over 8f at Standside (good) but struggles on soft (5/13, 0W0P); 83 days off adds to the question marks and her recent string of double-figure finishes makes confidence hard to find.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and 83 days off the track, Mags has experience of today's distance and going and catches the eye with a speed rating of 71 that outstrips her official mark, though a return to form is the obvious query.

runners_data.name: Carvalhal
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win on soft at 8f and a second over 7f, giving her the most directly relevant soft-ground form of the prominent types; 61 days off is manageable and Nicola Burns's 2lb claim is a useful asset.|
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner two starts back and second three starts back, giving him some solid recent form to work with, though unplaced efforts either side of that spell and 61 days off the track are notes of caution; has run over today's trip and going, carrying 138 lb from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Survivor's Code
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield slot by the density of closers in this field; a soft-ground winner over 7f is the key form line and its style-fit discount (0.92) reflects that it may not get the late run it needs today.|
runners_data.comment: Survivor's Code won four starts back but has since posted three disappointing efforts, and 106 days off the track adds an unknown fitness element; she has run over today's trip and going before, though 127 lb from stall 18 is no obvious help.

runners_data.name: Miss Americana
runners_data.note: True hold-up operator whose two soft-going placed efforts (2W, soft) give her a case on going but she has been crowded into a midfield mapping that doesn't reflect her natural rearward style; 81 days off adds risk.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 17 of 19 on our figures, Miss Americana faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's distance and going before and shaped with promise when second two starts back.

runners_data.name: Rampage
runners_data.note: Apprentice-ridden prominent type for McCourt (1/10 over 14 days); ran just seven days ago and has been finishing mid-table consistently, though a prominent pitch on today's soft surface keeps him honest for minor honours.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Rampage heads here just seven days after his latest fifth, and while he has run over today's trip and going before, carrying 124 lb from stall 17 alongside an official mark of 42 makes it hard to see him threatening from the midfield.

runners_data.name: Master Garvey
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose soft-going record is limited (4/15, 0W0P) and who has been placed rearward in the map by the sheer volume of closers; Terry Casey's 7lb claim is the main positive.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Master Garvey faces a stiff task here; a third three starts back offers a crumb of comfort, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but it is hard to make a case for him at these weights.

runners_data.name: Crosshaven
runners_data.note: A natural closer whose soft-going experience is thin (1/4) and who has been mapped to midfield purely because the field's hold-up quota is overcrowded; without a jockey listed and 74 days off, hard to make a case.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and returning after 74 days off, Crosshaven has experience of today's trip and ground but a string of sevenths and unplaced efforts make it hard to fancy him breaking the sequence from stall 12 off 137 lb.

runners_data.name: Limbocall
runners_data.note: Hold-up type trained by O'Callaghan (3/13 over 14 days, a positive) but soft-ground form is sparse (1/6) and a sequence of 0s in recent outings is a concern; the trainer's form is the only hook.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 15 of 19 on our figures, Limbocall faces a stiff task here; 48 days off the track is a concern, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Incredible Army
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old whose soft record is limited (2/8, 0W0P) and who carries a fading-in-finish flag; 38 days since last run and no jockey listed, making assessment difficult.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 16 of 19 on our figures, Incredible Army makes little appeal here, though he has winning form within his recent starts and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Lady Kelly
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly from JP Murtagh's yard (0/27 over 14 days is a significant negative); soft-ground form of 4/6 runs shows a placing but form figures include several poor efforts and the trainer stat is damning short-term.|
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back gives Lady Kelly a solid platform to threaten here, and she has experience of today's trip and going; ranked top of the field on our rating, she is a leading danger, though a trainer in the depths of a barren spell and 62 days off the track are the chief concerns.

runners_data.name: Lust
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type with a fade-in-finish flag and a style-fit discount (0.92); best soft run was a fifth over 8f but 75 days off and a string of double-figure finishes make it hard to enthuse despite soft being acceptable.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Lust does at least have experience over today's trip and going, and a third two starts back offers some encouragement, but 75 days off the track is a fitness concern and he faces a stiff task from a rating of 53.

runners_data.name: Bright Dick
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from a remarkable 782-day absence for Luke Comer; ran a placing on soft over 9f in his last completed season and a first run back for over two years demands caution, but his style suits if fitness is there.|
runners_data.comment: Bright Dick is yet to win in recent starts and faces a stiff ask returning after a 782-day absence, but he does bring experience over today's trip and a third last time out suggests some residual ability, even if unplaced efforts before that cloud the picture.

runners_data.name: Real Petite
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a fade-in-finish flag; won over 8f on good and the soft record (11/15) is poor — the redistribution into midfield reflects that she's a natural closer who may not get the run she needs.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 19 on our figures, Real Petite has posted an eighth and an unplaced run in her last two starts, making her hard to fancy despite the win four starts back. She has run over today's trip and going before, but the weight and draw offer little extra appeal.

runners_data.name: Tempted Angel
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning after 172 days off for Mark Fahey; form runs have all been on standard/tapeta and today's soft turf is an unknown, making the going query the central concern despite a handy racing style.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and returning after 172 days off, Tempted Angel faces a stiff task from stall 13 carrying 132 lb, and our figures rank her 18th of 19; experience over today's trip is about the best that can be said for her.

runners_data.name: Roderick
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up veteran whose soft record (10/15, 1W4P) is decent on volume but the win was distant; pushed into a midfield slot by the field's closer density, and at his age the emphasis is on whether he retains the ability rather than the position.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 81 days off, Roderick does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a runner-up finish last time out offers some encouragement, though carrying 130 lb from stall 14 while ranked 13 of 19 underlines the size of his task.

races.paceDynamic: Volendam is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 19-runner soft-ground mile and, crucially, faces no genuine challenger for the lead — Carvalhal, Rampage, Bright Dick, and Tempted Angel are the prominent types most likely to press close up behind, creating an orderly, sustainable gallop rather than a hot, contested pace. On soft ground at Gowran over a mile, a controlled early pace typically sets up a stamina-sapping grind in the final two furlongs, where position entering the straight becomes the decisive factor — horses that travel prominently without expending excess energy early hold a clear structural advantage. The field contains a heavy concentration of genuine hold-up types — Crosshaven, Lust, Limbocall, Roderick, and Real Petite among others are all natural closers squeezed rearward — and on a soft surface with a single unchallenged leader, the late ground they need to make up may simply not materialise. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit close to Volendam's sustainable pace and produce their effort in the straight without the energy cost of a big move from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Volendam Controls, Prominent Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Volendam sets a steady, uncontested gallop and the soft ground stretches closers beyond their range.
scenarios.body: Volendam dictates the fractions on soft ground and the race becomes a test of sustained stamina from the top two furlongs out; horses sitting close in second or third have the tactical advantage of covering the pace without the energy drain of a sweeping late move. Prominent types Carvalhal and Bright Dick are ideally placed to pounce as the leader is challenged, while Rampage and Tempted Angel offer each-way interest from handy positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Grinds Out Stayers
scenarios.trigger: If the heavy underfoot conditions slow the pace to the point where raw stamina over the final furlong is the only currency.
scenarios.body: The soft surface turns the closing stages into an endurance examination and horses with proven staying power on similar going assert regardless of position entering the straight. Selective Power's soft-ground form figures and Carvalhal's win on soft at eight furlongs both align with this scenario, while Medieval Night's stamina profile is worth noting.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Stays All The Way
scenarios.trigger: If Volendam's rivals underestimate the pace and allow the leader to steal a decisive break at the top of the straight.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing to commit to close Volendam down, the leader maintains rhythm through the final two furlongs and simply outstays a field that has given too much ground; soft ground paradoxically rewards the horse that has been saving energy by controlling the race from the front. Volendam's consistent prominence and apprentice claiming allowance make this a live outcome, though its style-fit flag tempers confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses badly in the straight and a wall of hold-up horses sweeps past the weakening leaders.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires most of the field's genuine closers — Crosshaven, Limbocall, Lust, Roderick — to secure a clean run and produce a coordinated late surge, which is structurally unlikely given their redistribution flags and the controlled pace Volendam sets. Selective Power and Miss Americana retain the best soft-ground credentials if the late rush does materialise, but with so many mapped out of their natural role, this remains the least probable shape.

watchPoints.text: Volendam sets off uncontested in front — if Jessica O'Gorman steals a decisive cushion by the two-furlong pole with no rival prepared to commit, the race may already be over before the closers can respond.

Carvalhal is the one prominent type with a direct soft-ground win over this trip — watch how Nicola Burns positions her off Volendam's pace in the first furlong, as sitting second or third could be the race-winning slot.

The going could tighten further during the card; the 4:30 run follows six races on soft and any deterioration to heavy-soft would bias the race even more heavily toward those who travel close to the pace and stay.

Bright Dick's 782-day absence is the most extreme layoff in the field — watch the market move if punters have stable intelligence, as a well-prepared return from Luke Comer on soft ground with a prominent style could make him dangerous.

Multiple hold-up types including Crosshaven, Limbocall, and Lust are all carrying redistribution flags — if they drift back to their natural rearward position from a wide or slow draw, traffic problems in the straight are likely for several runners simultaneously.

races.name: Support The Irish Injured Jockeys Fund Handicap

runners_data.name: Bill Silvers
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a tendency to fade in the closing stages; six-year-old has soft-going form but five of his last six runs ended outside the placings, and the visor hasn't unlocked an upturn — this field shape gives him little hope from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Bill Silvers has run over today's trip and going, our rating has him ranked top of the field, and he drops to stall one carrying 140 lb — yet his recent string of unplaced efforts and a pull-up make him difficult to trust for a horse yet to win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Bundle Of Interest
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type whose recent form reads 7-0779 without a placed effort on similar going; five-year-old apprentice booking and lack of soft-ground wins make this a tough ask in a competitive 19-runner mile handicap.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Bundle Of Interest does at least bring distance experience and a fitness edge having run just five days ago, and her rating of 77 gives her a case at 140 lb from stall 13.

runners_data.name: Lahore Da King
runners_data.note: Returned a 60-day absence and drops back to the mile after showing his best form at shorter; tongue-tie retained, and his sole win came on soft going at this trip — the layoff is the key risk but there is a relevant form line if fit.
runners_data.comment: Ran well to score in recent starts but has been unplaced in three of his last five outings, so consistency is the concern; he has run over today's distance and going before, and 60 days between runs leaves his current fitness open to question.

runners_data.name: Java Wood
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator with a course win at a mile on good; soft going is a step up in conditions but his profile suggests he handles it well enough, and trainer K Smith has limited recent runners to draw confidence from.
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back and a winner four starts back, Java Wood brings distance and going experience to the table, but he has been out of the frame in his last two outings and carries 139 lb from stall 19 — the recent form makes him hard to fancy at face value.

runners_data.name: Majestic King
runners_data.note: Another natural hold-up type who fades in the finish; his best placed efforts have come over further on good or softer, and 49 days off needs to be overcome — the soft ground could suit but the tendency to fade is a concern in a truly run race.
runners_data.comment: Majestic King showed a fourth last time out after a pair of unplaced efforts, though he did score five starts back, with experience over today's trip and going in his favour; the 49-day absence and a career-high weight of 138 lb from stall 17 are the chief concerns.

runners_data.name: Navagio
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer whose natural position is the rear of the field; seven-year-old was pushed to midfield on the map because the hold-up group is overcrowded — his soft-going record is poor and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.91) correctly tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Navagio nonetheless catches the eye with a rating of 75 that sits nine pounds clear of his official mark, suggesting he is better than his recent finishes imply, and he has experience over today's trip and going; the concern is that his form figures offer little encouragement heading in.

runners_data.name: Mr Perth
runners_data.note: Three-year-old on a mark of 66 with four runs, all landing outside the frame; a natural hold-up horse carrying a style-fit discount (0.90) from a forced midfield position, and with no soft-ground wins in his short career, the evidence is thin.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 13 of 19 on our ratings, Mr Perth faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a 32-day break carrying 131 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Merciless
runners_data.note: 155-day break is a significant flag, and his form at Dundalk and Sligo on standard ground is hard to translate to soft Gowran; true hold-up style makes this a difficult assignment even fresh, and the style-fit flag (0.92) correctly tempers his chance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 17 of 19 on our figures, Merciless has been well held in recent outings and returns after a 155-day absence, making her hard to fancy despite having run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Funk
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse by nature, shown in midfield by redistribution only; his best effort was a second at the Curragh on heavy, so soft ground is not a worry, but the STYLE_FIT discount (0.91) and a crowded rear will make positioning difficult.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Cosmic Funk does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and his speed rating holds up reasonably well against this field, but a five-day turnaround and a tendency to finish mid-to-rear makes stepping forward a tough ask from stall two.

runners_data.name: Aurora Mist
runners_data.note: Holds a win on good at the mile and was placed here before; naturally held up but redistributed to midfield — the soft going is the main unknown, and while trainer Andrew Slattery is in good form (T14: 5/17), her soft-ground record is modest.
runners_data.comment: Two consecutive unplaced finishes make Aurora Mist hard to fancy on recent form, and she ranks 18th of 19 on our figures; the win three starts back offers faint hope, and she does have experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Green Kite
runners_data.note: A hold-up type with a tendency to fade; no jockey listed in the data which is a minor flag, and her soft-going placed efforts have come over shorter — the STYLE_FIT discount (0.90) and finish tendency make her unattractive from a shape perspective.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 14 of 19 on our figures, Green Kite faces a stiff task from stall 12 carrying 132 lb, though a second two starts back and experience over today's trip and going offer slim grounds for mild interest.

runners_data.name: Faoladh
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in the field and the pivot on which the entire race shape turns; his recent win came over 7f on good at Gowran so the step to a soft mile is a genuine query, but the lack of any pace rival makes his tactical advantage extraordinary.
runners_data.comment: Faoladh won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims, but two unplaced efforts before that win and a rating of 71 suggest he can be inconsistent, and 141 lb from stall ten adds to the query.

runners_data.name: Suir Monad
runners_data.note: Listed as uncertain style (U) with only three career runs, all producing placings at 8f or 7f on good or soft — compact form makes him hard to assess but he sits in a useful prominent-to-midfield position under a powerful yard (Slattery, T14: 5/17).
runners_data.comment: Consistent without a win in his last three starts, Suir Monad returns third last time out and brings distance and going experience to the table; rated 78 by us and drawn four off a 31-day break, the chief risk is converting that placed form into something more decisive.

runners_data.name: Rhythm King
runners_data.note: Six-year-old whose soft-going profile is actually decent despite a poor recent run tally; pushed to midfield from a true hold-up role by the redistribution process — the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) is warranted and his best form has come over longer trips.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Rhythm King does bring distance and going experience to the table, and 33 days off suggests connections have had time to find a spark, though his recent string of unplaced efforts make it hard to fancy him from stall 18 carrying 136 lb.

runners_data.name: She's Ideal
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins over 10f on good, now dropping to a soft mile — the trip shortening is a question mark, but she is the most in-form prominent runner in the field and her recent trajectory gives her a strong profile to challenge Faoladh from close range.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures and drawn in stall 14, She's Ideal faces a stiff ask, though she does arrive on the back of a third last time out following back-to-back wins, and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Gloriously Glam
runners_data.note: Proven prominent performer with a pipe-and-slippers booking of Colin Keane; two wins in her last five starts and placed at this trip on soft before — she is the second-most likely horse to take advantage of the front-runner's position if Faoladh weakens.
runners_data.comment: Gloriously Glam has run over today's trip and going, and her second two starts back shows she retains ability, though an unplaced effort last time out and a rating of 65 officially leave her with ground to make up from stall nine carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Goofy Gander
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse who relishes coming from off the pace; 83 days off is a concern and he has no wins in five career starts, but soft going at 5f up (7f record) and a strong yard (Harrington) suggest he could outrun his odds if traffic clears.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and returning after 83 days off, Goofy Gander has experience over today's trip and going but has shown little consistency, with a best recent finish of fifth — she carries 135 lb from stall 11 for a stable needing improvement.

runners_data.name: Yutori
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer by nature pushed to midfield on the map; best effort was a second at Dundalk on standard, and his one soft-going run produced a 13th — the STYLE_FIT flag (0.91) is justified, and the trip and conditions both look uncertain.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 16 of 19 on our figures, Yutori faces a stiff ask from stall 16 carrying 135 lb, and an unplaced effort last time out does little to inspire confidence; experience over today's trip is the sole crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Unidos
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type with a finish-fading flag, currently repositioned to midfield through redistribution; three-year-old with no wins and no placings on soft ground, and a STYLE_FIT score of 0.91 underlines that his best chance depends on conditions he hasn't yet mastered.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Unidos makes for a difficult proposition, though he has run over today's trip before and returns on a fresh enough note just 10 days after his latest outing.

races.paceDynamic: Faoladh is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 19-horse field and, crucially, faces no credible pace rival — She's Ideal and Gloriously Glam are the only genuine prominent types, meaning Faoladh can stride into a soft, uncontested lead from the gates. On soft ground over a flat mile at Gowran, that scenario is potent: the race will be run at a sustainable rhythm, with Faoladh controlling every yard while the large hold-up contingent queues up behind, their ground-losing runs compromised by traffic in the straight. This shape heavily favours the lead and prominent profiles, as those horses will be closest to the gallop's pace without having burned energy to claim the position. The field contains a disproportionate number of hold-up horses — Navagio, Unidos, Rhythm King, Merciless, Cosmic Funk and others are true hold-up types repositioned to midfield on the map, with Navagio and Rhythm King most likely to secure the nearest available ground behind the front three simply on the basis of recent form and jockey profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Faoladh Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Faoladh secures the lead unopposed and sets a controlled, soft-ground-appropriate tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Faoladh controls from flag to finish at a metronomic pace, reaching the home turn in front and kicking into the straight with a length or more in hand; on soft ground a lone front-runner at a fair pace is notoriously hard to reel in, and She's Ideal and Gloriously Glam, sitting closest in the slipstream, are the likeliest challengers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If She's Ideal or Gloriously Glam track Faoladh closely and use their prominent berth to collar the leader entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: She's Ideal arrives with recent course-and-distance form and back-to-back wins, making her the most dangerous prominent-style challenger to Faoladh; Gloriously Glam, ridden by Colin Keane and proven at the trip in soft, is ideally placed to pounce if Faoladh ties up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and the race becomes a genuine stamina test, favouring horses with proven soft-ground staying power.
scenarios.body: In this shape, the race is run at an uneven gallop before grinding in the final two furlongs, which suits horses with durable soft-ground form over the mile rather than those with a turn of foot; Majestic King and Lahore Da King, both with soft-ground placed form at the trip, could emerge from the pack if attrition bites.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is deceptively strong early and Faoladh's lead collapses, opening a furlong-long sprint for held-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: This scenario is structurally unlikely because most of the hold-up horses have been redistributed from their natural position and face a significant traffic problem in a 19-runner field on a flat track; Goofy Gander and Java Wood, both genuine hold-up types with soft-ground experience at this distance, are the best-placed of the closers if gaps appear.

watchPoints.text: Faoladh is the fulcrum of the entire race — if he travels smoothly on the soft mile and isn't pressured by She's Ideal or Gloriously Glam in the first three furlongs, he could prove very difficult to catch from the front.

She's Ideal is in career-best form with two consecutive wins and arrives as the most likely prominent challenger to Faoladh; watch whether Adam Caffrey positions her immediately behind the leader before the home turn.

With 19 runners on soft ground, traffic is a serious risk for the large group of hold-up horses — Goofy Gander, Java Wood and Cosmic Funk are all likely to encounter interference in the straight, and their chances depend heavily on a clear run.

Gloriously Glam's soft-going record (11th in her only comparable conditions run) needs monitoring against her overall prominently-ridden form; if the ground proves too testing, Colin Keane may find her lacking her usual turn of foot.

Trainer Andrew Slattery saddles three runners (Faoladh, Aurora Mist, Suir Monad) on the back of a 5/17 T14 strike rate — stable form is live, and jockey deployments across the trio are worth noting for any late-market moves.

races.name: Racing Again September 19th Maiden

runners_data.name: Antrim Coast
runners_data.note: Prominent-style performer with solid course form (2nd over 22f at Gowran) and similar-going credentials; tracking the lone front-runner from a handy position is exactly what suits this horse, and 32 days between runs looks a clean preparation.|

runners_data.name: Banbridge
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's 10-year-old returns after 143 days off but boasts three wins from five in similar going and placed form at 24f; the long absence is the only query against an otherwise well-suited profile in trip and conditions.|

runners_data.name: Bartholomew
runners_data.note: Won over 16f at Gowran in good form and handles the track well; the headgear note and four-year-old's limited soft-ground exposure are minor flags, but Martin Brassil sends very few runners and a single entry here merits respect.|

runners_data.name: Dee Bee Zed
runners_data.note: Won over 16f at Gowran and has gone well fresh before; the prominent style is ideal for tracking Navy Guitar, and with only two career starts on record there is significant unknown upside — the stable's T14 strike rate of 1/10 is modest but the horse's own profile is straightforward.|

runners_data.name: Figero
runners_data.note: Thomas Mullins' five-year-old has form figures that include a win over 16f at Gowran but also a 13th on soft; a true hold-up horse who has been placed into the midfield map due to overcrowding at the rear, meaning it is likely to race further back than ideal, which tempers its prospects in a shape that will be decided by those up with the pace.|

runners_data.name: Joe Cool
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent-to-placed performer who has finished second twice in soft ground and brings Colin Keane aboard, which is an obvious positive; the step up to 1m6f on soft is a new test for a horse whose best form has come at shorter trips.|

runners_data.name: Navy Guitar
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in the field, returning after 325 days off for Diego Dias, whose single runner at the meeting is notable; the long absence is a real concern, but if fit, an uncontested lead on soft ground makes this horse the pivotal pace-setter the entire tactical picture revolves around.|

runners_data.name: Path d'Oroux
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's nine-year-old is a genuine hold-up type with a placed run over 14f at Gowran but a 15th and 11th in recent outings paint a difficult picture; nothing in the profile suggests it can overcome a poor draw in the queue from the rear in this race shape.|

runners_data.name: Western Fold
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's seven-year-old won over 25f at Gowran and has three wins plus placed form across 20-25f in soft-to-good conditions — the stamina profile is undeniable; racing off a 126-day break is a concern, but this is the most credible hold-up threat if the late surge scenario materialises.|

runners_data.name: Ballybawn Belter
runners_data.note: Liz Doyle's eight-year-old won over 20f at Haydock and was placed on soft at 21f at Leopardstown — the form in similar conditions is solid; however, this is a horse whose natural style is at the rear of the field, and having been mapped to midfield due to overcrowding, it may find itself in an unnatural position that blunts its finishing kick.|

runners_data.name: Fraher Field
runners_data.note: Consistent placed horse over 16-17f at Gowran with a second on two occasions — the track suits; a genuine hold-up horse whose style means it wants to come from well back, yet with so many horses filling that role in this field it will struggle to find daylight, and the STYLE_FIT flag is well-earned.|

runners_data.name: Kaleo Ametsa
runners_data.note: Josh Halley's six-year-old has finished third on one occasion but no better, and the headgear note signals something is being tried to help; no soft-going wins on record and the hold-up style places it firmly in the group that will need a late surge that this race shape is unlikely to produce.|

runners_data.name: Run For Mahler
runners_data.note: Won over 20f at Gowran from hold-up and has recent form (7-6-7) that reflects a horse running into a wall; Adam Caffrey takes the ride and the headgear is on, but three consecutive poor finishes make it hard to argue for improvement in a competitive field.|

runners_data.name: Thisistheway
runners_data.note: Yvonne Latta's seven-year-old was placed twice at 16-20f at Gowran and has Ben Coen aboard, who is one of the better jockeys in the field; the prominent style is well-suited to tracking Navy Guitar, and the form string showing places at this course gives it a legitimate tactical claim.|

runners_data.name: Nothingbutadream
runners_data.note: Racing just one day after a previous run is an immediate red flag — freshness is non-existent; the form figures of 0-0-7-0 tell a grim story, the fade-in-finish warning is consistent with those figures, and soft ground over 1m6f represents a significant stamina test for a four-year-old out of form.|

runners_data.name: Goodie Girl
runners_data.note: Dermot McLoughlin's eight-year-old won over 19f at Gowran and showed placed form in soft ground previously — the course and conditions are not a problem; a natural hold-up horse placed into the midfield map because the rear of the field is overcrowded, so the horse may not get the patient ride it needs, reducing its chance of producing its best.|

runners_data.name: Set To Win
runners_data.note: Luke Comer's five-year-old ran once 818 days ago over 6f at Gowran and has never been seen since — that is an extraordinary absence and the sole piece of form is over a trip dramatically shorter than 1m6f; the fade-in-finish tag and lightly-raced flag together make this a horse to treat with extreme caution on debut over this extreme trip.|

races.paceDynamic: Navy Guitar is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 17-horse field and, critically, faces no genuine pressure from another pace-setter at this trip — on soft ground over 1m6f at Gowran, that amounts to a sustainable, likely-unchallenged lead. Antrim Coast, Banbridge, Dee Bee Zed, Thisistheway and Bartholomew are all prominent-style horses who will queue up behind Navy Guitar rather than challenge for the front, creating a tight, bunched mid-group rather than a strung-out field. The redistribution of Goodie Girl, Fraher Field, Figero and Ballybawn Belter into the midfield map is a consequence of overcrowding at the rear, not a reflection of their natural forward intent; the horses most likely to actually secure prominent positions ahead of them are the confirmed P-types named above. With soft ground slowing the tempo and a single front-runner controlling fractions from flag to finish, this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-mid horses who can track the leader in a good position and sustain their effort through the testing ground — genuine hold-up horses who are forced further back than ideal will be swimming against the tactical tide.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Navy Guitar Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Navy Guitar gets an uncontested lead and controls a measured pace on soft, setting up a test of stamina from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Navy Guitar dictates every fraction, and the soft ground combined with a lone pace-setter creates a race where those positioned close enough to attack before the final turn hold the decisive advantage; prominent trackers who can sustain their effort get first run on the field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group collectively move up to apply pressure on Navy Guitar entering the straight, triggering an earlier test of stamina.
scenarios.body: The pace quickens two furlongs out as several prominent horses make simultaneous moves, spreading the race wide and rewarding the best stayer in the field who has conserved energy just behind the leader; class and stamina become the decisive factors.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Staying Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow enough to compress the field and hold-up horses find a clearer-than-expected passage from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Western Fold, the most proven stayer in the field with multiple wins at 20f-plus in similar conditions, represents the most credible late challenger if the closers are not simply too far back; Ballybawn Belter and Fraher Field are the other hold-up types with the profile to benefit, though their redistribution into midfield rather than genuine rear positions tempers optimism.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Nullifies Frontrunner
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes significant interference or traffic issues in the straight that disrupts Navy Guitar's rhythm and collapses the pace advantage.
scenarios.body: With 17 runners on soft ground over an extended trip, the combination of stamina-sapping conditions and traffic congestion could see an unexpectedly strong finisher emerge from the midfield pack; this shape remains unlikely given the absence of any pressing pace to collapse, but Joe Cool's consistent placed form at both soft and good provides a modest claim.

watchPoints.text: Navy Guitar's fitness after 325 days off is the single most important factor in this race — if the front-runner is not at peak condition, the uncontested lead scenario collapses entirely and prominent trackers like Antrim Coast and Thisistheway inherit the race without a true pace-setter to follow.

With 17 runners on soft ground at Gowran over 1m6f, watch for significant traffic interference in the straight — horses like Fraher Field, Goodie Girl and Ballybawn Belter, who need a clear passage from the rear, are most at risk of finding trouble in running.

Nothingbutadream racing just one day after its previous outing is highly unusual and worth flagging — monitor market moves; if it drifts sharply in the betting it is likely a non-trier or at serious risk of being exhausted early, which could disrupt the pace if it breaks fast.|

Western Fold returns from 126 days off for Gordon Elliott with a strong stamina profile over 20-25f — watch whether it is well-backed in the market, as a freshened-up Elliott runner with that record in soft could be flying under the radar at a big price.

The cluster of prominent-style horses (Antrim Coast, Banbridge, Dee Bee Zed, Thisistheway, Bartholomew) all wanting to sit just behind Navy Guitar in a field of 17 creates a risk of early crowding and jostling for position — watch for any of these horses being shuffled back against their will in the first quarter-mile, as that would significantly alter their chance.
